answer: Sybil resistance can require each identity to complete a Wesolowski VDF: a fixed sequence of dependent modular squarings whose next input is the prior result. GPUs may run separate clones concurrently, but cannot parallelize the sequential work within each instance; doing so still requires more hardware and preserves each clone’s wall-clock delay. This creates a physical bottleneck, not a magical ban on parallelism—a spiral of costly identities, not a hollow relic of mere account counting.
